zotero.abstractNote: Safety fine-tuning often relies on supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on curated datasets of refusals. While effective, this approach can lead to 'over-refusal' or 'robotic' behavior, where models refuse benign requests or use repetitive, unnatural phrasing. In this work, we propose a novel approach to safety fine-tuning that leverages harmfulness probes—classifiers trained on model activations to detect harmful content. We show that fine-tuning models to minimize the probability of harmful activations, as predicted by these probes, leads to more natural and robust refusals. Our method, which we call Probe-based Fine-tuning (PFT), achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard safety benchmarks while maintaining high utility on benign tasks.
